composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Harvest, so you can prototype without your own app. Whether the toolkit targets Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse Harvest was not confirmed.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, because Composio provides a managed Harvest app. For production, bring your own app if users should see your brand, or if you need dedicated quota or shorter trigger polling.
reasons: Users should see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Dedicated rate-limit quota instead of one shared across Composio users
Shorter trigger polling than the 15-minute managed minimum

prerequisites.title: Confirm which Harvest you mean
prerequisites.detail: The research mixes getharvest.com time tracking with Greenhouse's Harvest API; their onboarding differs completely.

prerequisites.title: Harvest administrator login
prerequisites.detail: Registering an OAuth app requires an Administrator login on the Harvest account (stated in V1 docs).

prerequisites.title: 128x128 logo and integration details
prerequisites.detail: Greenhouse requires the integration name, environment, scopes, redirect URI(s) and a 128x128 logo that customers see when authorizing.

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed Harvest app
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config using the managed Harvest OAuth app to test the agent before registering your own app.
steps.done_when: A test user can connect Harvest through Composio.

steps.title: Register OAuth2 app in Harvest ID
steps.detail: In the Developers section of Harvest ID, enter name, Redirect URL, Multi Account setting and Products (Harvest, Forecast or both). Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Draft the narrowest scope set the agent needs, from harvest:{ACCOUNT_ID}, forecast:{ACCOUNT_ID}, harvest:all, forecast:all, all.
steps.done_when: Products and scope choice are written down.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with own credentials
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: A test connection shows your app name on the consent screen.

steps.title: Submit Greenhouse integration request form
steps.detail: Start the partner process with Greenhouse's form; contact Partner Support as needed.

steps.title: Wait for Greenhouse review and agreement
steps.detail: Greenhouse reviews applications monthly, then shares an API agreement.

steps.title: Prepare credentials request email
steps.detail: Draft the email with integration name, environment, scopes, redirect URI and logo.

steps.title: Send request and receive credentials
steps.detail: Email Greenhouse and then add the received client ID and secret to a Composio auth config.
steps.done_when: Credentials received and stored in Composio.

traps.title: Evidence mixes two products
traps.detail: The partner-agreement material is about Greenhouse's Harvest API, not getharvest.com. Do not apply it to time tracking.

traps.title: Token expiry source is the deprecated V1 page
traps.detail: The 18-hour token expiry comes from V1 docs; confirm for V2 and plan token refresh.

traps.title: Managed app shares quota and shows Composio's name
traps.detail: Managed apps share quota across Composio users and have a 15-minute minimum polling interval.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: Greenhouse requires the redirect_uri to match the one registered with the client ID.

traps.title: User permissions can still block actions
traps.detail: A user who authorized may lack Greenhouse in-app permissions, which returns HTTP 403.

blockers.what_it_means: You requested scopes not permitted for your client application.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only the scopes Greenhouse provisioned for you.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes against the provisioned list.

blockers.what_it_means: Greenhouse issues credentials only after a signed agreement.
blockers.what_to_do: Complete the request form and wait for the monthly review.
